Fast and slow vehicle classes only.
Good environment and right-hand traffic norm.
No human fatigue/distraction and no crashes except breakdown.

contributions.summary: Discretizes lane, time, and vehicle state for traffic simulation.
Uses Poisson arrivals and lambda to vary traffic load.
Adds PIEV and velocity-dependent stochastic acceleration/deceleration.
Separates overtaking probability, gap conditions, and danger.
Compares priority rules and a collision-avoidance override.
Compares four metrics across lanes, inflow, and rules.
Proposes 1.5 vehicles/s rule switching under strong intelligent-control assumptions.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Symbols and units are declared in Table 1.
Pa/Pb probabilities are assigned by vehicle type and velocity.
Scenario inflow, lane count, and speed limits are selected inputs.
MATLAB loop, warm-up, density window, and event counters define extraction.

dependency_graph.closure_status: Positive model interfaces are explicit, but parameter calibration, danger implementation, code completeness, and uncertainty remain unresolved.
edges: Cell state and gap variables feed stochastic arrival placement and current vehicle state.
Generated vehicles, types, initial speeds, and lanes enter following decisions.
Following speed, gap, and leader state enter overtaking intent and safety calculations.
Overtaking feasibility and danger side effects are routed through keep-right or unrestricted priority rules.
Rule actions update the lane matrix used by the implementation and metric extraction.
Scenario velocity, density, passing, and danger comparisons motivate the intelligent extension.
Modified response and rule tables are evaluated through the same metric extraction loop.
feedbacks: Metric comparisons motivate the intelligent rule switch.

independent_extensions.summary: Use a normalized Poisson law including N=0 and calibrate lambda from arrival data.
Run spatial/temporal refinement and seeded repeated simulations.
Calibrate friction, gap acceptance, and side-risk weights with observed lane-change data.
Publish all helper functions and reconcile code with displayed rules and metrics.
Sweep inflow, lane count, speed limit, and rule weights with uncertainty intervals.
Fit an intelligent controller and optimize the threshold under speed, density, and safety objectives.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A compact method-metric-policy route may improve traceability; no judge source proves causality.
A staged implementation and spatiotemporal diagram may make a complex traffic simulation auditable.
A thresholded policy may make model outputs actionable, but its threshold remains source-specific.

models.summary: MU-A-2014-25142-001: Represent lanes, cells, vehicle states, and one-second movement updates.
MU-A-2014-25142-002: Generate stochastic arrivals and traffic-load scenarios.
MU-A-2014-25142-003: Choose acceleration, deceleration, or maintenance from gap and velocity-dependent probabilities.
MU-A-2014-25142-004: Decide overtaking, compute lane-change safety, and aggregate a road danger index.
MU-A-2014-25142-005: Compare keep-right and unrestricted rules and add density/collision safeguards.
MU-A-2014-25142-006: Run two/three-lane, rule, speed-limit, and intelligent scenarios and extract velocity, density, passing, and danger outputs.
MU-A-2014-25142-007: Choose keep-right at low inflow and unrestricted at high inflow under assumed intelligent control.

results_trace.summary: Keep-right helps tested two-lane velocity; unrestricted can win tested heavy three-lane cases.
Keep-right concentrates vehicles in right lanes.
Keep-right increases total passing and right-side passing risk.
Danger proxy peaks at middle density and is lower under keep-right in tested cases.
Velocity pattern remains similar while higher speed limits raise danger.

weaknesses.summary: Four-meter cells and one-second update are coarse.
Friction force/coefficient and linear approximation are not dimensionally/calibrationally closed.
ad algebra is not transparently derived from ap and V1.
Gs coefficient changes from 2.8 to 3.4 without independent calibration.
D is called an average but Eq.15 shows only a sum.
A=3 right-pass multiplier is weakly sourced.
Code line truncation and missing helpers block reproduction.
Code and prose do not fully reconcile velocity/density/danger units and extraction.
Three speed limits are not a global uncertainty study.
Safety is reduced to speed under no-crash assumption.
0.1 s response and changed tables lack data calibration.
Joint speed-safety recommendation lacks calibrated utility.
Some values are estimated from common sense.
Appendix closes without a complete executable archive.

writing_logic.summary: Method -> submodels -> scenarios -> metrics -> conditional policy.
Symbols -> terminology -> physical and behavioral boundary.
Random arrival -> lambda -> scenario mapping -> simplification.
PIEV -> state read -> safe gap -> probability -> executable rules.
Intent -> target gap -> lane-change physics -> danger metric.
Simple baseline -> lane/rule extensions -> scenario output.
Metric choice -> figure -> observation -> mechanism -> rule implication.
Speed perturbation -> pattern stability -> safety caveat.
Mirror transfer -> intelligent assumptions -> modified rules -> light/heavy result.
